''Protasparagus virgatus'' ([[John Gilbert Baker|Baker]]) Oberm. }} '''''Asparagus virgatus''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Asparagaceae]] family.{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:531381-1 |title= Asparagus virgatus Baker |author= |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=July 15, 2020}} It indigenous to South Eastern Africa. It is also known as '''tree fern''', '''tiki fern''',Florida Agriculture http://www.florida-agriculture.com/consumers/tree_fern.htm and '''African broom fern'''.Plant Database {{cite web|url=http://www.plantdatabase.co.za/Asparagus_virgatus |title=Asparagus virgatus - African broom fern |accessdate=2011-11-16 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406030818/http://www.plantdatabase.co.za/Asparagus_virgatus |archivedate=2012-04-06 }} ''Asparagus virgatus'' is a member of the genus ''[[Asparagus (genus)|Asparagus]]'', and not a true [[fern]]. ==Description== The plant grows several fine bushy stems with needle like leaves, reaching over one meter in length. This [[perennial plant]] produces small white flowers during spring, and small spherical red fruits that then turn black as they mature. This plant can be found growing in the shady undergrowth, especially along rivers. Although water loving, this plant is able to survive with little water. ==Uses== Unlike edible ''[[Asparagus officinalis]]'', ''A. virgatus'' has little or no nutritional value to people. ===Cut flower industry=== ''A. virgatus'' is of commercial value, used world wide in the [[cut flower]] industry as [[foliage]]. The plant produces attractive green bushy stems with fine needle like leaves. When combined with [[rose]], [[gerbera]], and other focal flowers it forms an attractive floral display. Vase life is typically two weeks. High quality stems can be identified by the fresh green color, and stem length. Major producing areas include [[South Africa]], [[Central America]], [[Florida]], [[Israel]], and the [[Near East]]. ==References== {{reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q4807701}} [[Category:Asparagus|virgatus]] [[Category:Flora of Southern Africa]] [[Category:Taxa named by John Gilbert Baker]]
